guardian.title: At least 44 dead after overcrowded ferry capsizes on Lake Kariba in Zimbabwe
guardian.description:
Operation under way to rescue dozens missing after boat overturned by waves at world’s largest human-made lake

At least 44 people have died after an overcrowded ferry capsized on Lake Kariba in Zimbabwe, police said.

The boat had a capacity of 90 people, but was carrying 114 adult passengers, five crew members and an unknown number of children, Zimbabwe’s civil protection unit (CPU) said earlier on Wednesday, citing ticket sales.

guardian.description:
South African scientist’s breakthrough research shows soil fungus could be used in fight against devastating crop pest

Hearing about fields full of dead caterpillars enveloped in a mysterious white substance intrigued the South African scientist Letodi Luki Mathulwe. Something was killing off the African armyworm – one of the most devastating pests for farmers in east and southern Africa.

guardian.title: Spain to introduce temporary border checks on visitors from Italy
guardian.description:
Move comes in response to Rome imposing similar measures after mass migration rush to Ceuta

Spain has announced it will introduce temporary border checks on visitors from Italy in response to Rome imposing similar measures after a mass rush of people from Morocco into Ceuta.

The checks, which come “amid the persistent irregular migration pressure” facing Italy, will start at midnight on Saturday and last until 7 September, Spain’s interior ministry said in a statement.

guardian.title: Ebola virus behind massive outbreak in DRC could be mutating, officials say
guardian.description:
Cases have passed 4,000 and health watchdog plans to go door to door to find patients in major response escalation

The virus causing a massive outbreak of Ebola in the Democratic Republic of the Congo could be mutating, health officials fear, as confirmed cases pass 4,000.

Africa’s public health watchdog said the time for incremental action was over as they announced plans to scale up every aspect of the response and go “door to door” looking for patients.

guardian.description:
Female staff alleged company failed to maintain safe workplace, after allegations of sexual assault against pilot

The Canadian airline WestJet has agreed to pay C$4.5m (£2.4m) to settle a decade-long sexual harassment class action lawsuit levelled by its female flight attendants, who alleged the company failed to maintain a safe workplace.

More than 100 people died after a powerful earthquake struck western Colombia, collapsing and severely damaging scores of buildings in major cities including Cali and Pereira.

Thailand has suspended firearms licences after the deadly Nonthaburi school shooting, as the bodies of the teenage attacker and the grandparents he killed were cremated.

guardian.description:
Forecasters warned the Chinese capital could receive more than one-third of its average annual rainfall over 24 hours

Thousands of people have been evacuated from areas at risk of flooding and landslides in Beijing, as the remnants of Typhoon Dolphin continue to bring torrential rain to northern and central China.

guardian.description:
The Comac C919 will fly from Beijing to Ulaanbaatar in Mongolia, although experts say it could take generations for it to challenge the west’s dominance of the industry

China hopes to break into the world of commercial aviation with the first international flight of a Chinese-made passenger jet scheduled for Wednesday.

The Comac C919 will take off from Beijing capital international airport at 3pm, landing in Ulaanbaatar, the capital of Mongolia, just over two hours later.

guardian.description:
Drought and wildfires intensify across continent, while tropical storms bring heavy rain and disruption to east Asia

guardian.description:
Organisers says new rule will ensure contest provides ‘safe and welcoming environment’ for participants

Broadcasters will no longer be eligible to host the Eurovision song contest if their state is involved in an “armed conflict” or “sensitive geopolitical situation”.

Eurovision is traditionally hosted by the previous year’s winning broadcaster, with the next show due to take place in Bulgaria in 2027 after singer Dara’s victory for the country in May.

rfi.title: Russia threatens retaliatory seizures of EU ships amid new sanctions push
rfi.description: Russian President Vladimir Putin on Wednesday threatened to seize ships belonging to European countries in retaliation for plans to sell off cargo seized from Russian "shadow fleet" vessels.

rfi.title: French ambassador to CAR disciplined over misconduct allegations
rfi.description: France’s foreign ministry has launched disciplinary proceedings against its ambassador to the Central African Republic, following allegations that he repeatedly brought young women to the official residence in Bangui and had sexual relations with some of them.

rfi.title: France gripped by latest summer heatwave as drought conditions worsen
rfi.description: Scorching heat continued to spread across most of mainland France on Wednesday, as the Ministry for Ecological Transition met to take stock of the effects of a drought that has been steadily worsening since May.

rfi.title: Hungary elects Orban critic Andras Baka as first president in new political era
rfi.description: Hungarian lawmakers on Tuesday approved former supreme court chief Andras Baka – a prominent critic of Viktor Orban who was ousted during the ex-premier's time in power – as the country's next head of state.

rfi.title: Total solar eclipse over Spain to draw millions of viewers across Europe
rfi.description: Large parts of north and central Spain, plus smaller parts of Portugal, Greenland and Iceland, will see a total solar eclipse on Wednesday – with the phenomenon also visible in the south of France. Starting near the North Pole before tracking south, the total eclipse will last up to two minutes and 18 seconds, with the partial eclipse visible across much of Western Europe, including the United Kingdom, Belgium, Switzerland and northern Italy.

rfi.title: Assisted dying, social media and agriculture put France’s top court in spotlight
rfi.description: France’s Constitutional Council is facing a politically charged end to the summer, with judges due to rule on a series of high-profile laws – including those covering assisted dying, social media use by children, agriculture and public security.

rfi.title: Race to find Ebola vaccine as DR Congo outbreak kills more than 2,000
rfi.description: The latest outbreak of Ebola has killed more than 2,000 people in the Democratic Republic of Congo, according to health authorities. Meanwhile, international efforts have been stepped up to test a vaccine for the highly contagious haemorrhagic fever.

rfi.title: Lebanon becomes first country in Middle East to abolish death penalty
rfi.description: Lebanon’s parliament on Tuesday abolished the death penalty, making it the first country in the Middle East to replace capital punishment with a sentence of life imprisonment with hard labour.

rfi.title: Former Syrian leader Assad sentenced to death in absentia over war crimes
rfi.description: A Syrian court on Tuesday sentenced former ruler Bashar al-Assad to death after a trial in absentia, convicting him of atrocities committed during the country's civil war. Six of his closest aides were also handed death sentences.

rfi.title: France and EU join international aid effort after Colombia earthquake
rfi.description: France has joined the European Union and a host of countries in offering assistance to Colombia, where volunteers and rescuers are searching for survivors following Monday's deadly earthquake.

rfi.title: May ’68 protest leader Cohn-Bendit pledges support to Glucksmann for 2027
rfi.description: Former Green MEP Daniel Cohn-Bendit, a historic figure on the French left, on Monday gave his support to Raphaël Glucksmann for France’s 2027 presidential election, in an interview with Le Point magazine.

rfi.title: Rebel forces in Ethiopia's Tigray state condemn army drone strikes
rfi.description: Rebel authorities on Tuesday accused the Ethiopian government of carrying out deadly drone strikes in southern Tigray state and condemned the move as "a serious escalation", amid fears of a new war.

rfi.title: France introduces tough fines for unsolicited telemarketing calls
rfi.description: France has banned unsolicited telemarketing calls under a new law to protect consumers and shield vulnerable people from fraudulent commercial practices. Individuals who make illegal calls can be fined up to €75,000 per call when the new law comes into effect on Tuesday.

rfi.title: Iran says ‘Muslim Nato’ pact reflects retreat from US security umbrella
rfi.description: Tehran has played down concerns over a new mutual defence pact between Saudi Arabia, Turkey and Pakistan, while portraying the agreement as evidence of declining regional reliance on the United States.

rfi.title: Moscow and Damascus reach deal over Russian military bases in Syria
rfi.description: Syria said on Sunday it had reached a deal with Moscow on the fate of Russia's two bases in the country, which it once used to provide military support to ousted leader Bashar al-Assad during the Syrian civil war.

rfi.title: Record temperatures swept regions home to 900 million people in July
rfi.description: Regions home to around 900 million people experienced their hottest July on record in 2026, including areas in the Sahel, Central America, France and Spain, according to analysis of Copernicus data.

rfi.title: Ghana backs Jamaica's petition to push UK for slavery reparations
rfi.description: Jamaica and Ghana, both former British colonies subjected to the transatlantic slave trade, are presenting a united front in the drive for reparatory justice. As Kingston prepares to lodge a formal petition with King Charles III seeking to advance its claim for reparations from the United Kingdom, Ghana's president says the global movement to address the legacy of slavery has reached a "defining moment".

rfi.title: Outsiders Malawi beat Ghana to reach WAFCON semi-finals and World Cup
rfi.description: Malawi have completed one of the biggest surprises in Women’s Africa Cup of Nations history, coming from behind to beat Ghana 2-1 and secure both a place in the semi-finals and qualification for the 2027 Women’s World Cup.

lemonde.title: EN DIRECT, éclipse solaire : le phénomène atteint progressivement son maximum en France métropolitaine ; l’éclipse totale commence en Espagne
lemonde.description: Une éclipse partielle du Soleil est observable en France métropolitaine, ce soir depuis 19 h 20. Elle sera quasi totale à Biarritz avec 99,5 % d’obscuration. En Espagne, l’intégralité du disque solaire sera masquée par la Lune, donnant lieu à une éclipse totale. Il est impératif de porter des lunettes de protection conformes pour l’observer.

lemonde.title: EN DIRECT, canicule : 80 départements seront placés en vigilance orange jeudi ; des températures encore « très élevées » au moment de l’éclipse solaire, en particulier dans l’Ouest
lemonde.description: Au total en Europe, au moins 92 millions de personnes devraient connaître des températures supérieures à 35 °C à un moment de la journée mercredi, dont 30 millions en France, selon l’AFP. Vers 20 heures, les températures seront souvent comprises entre 30 °C et 35 °C, entre 25 °C et 28 °C le long de la Manche, a fait savoir Météo-France.

lemonde.title: En Libye, le retour diplomatique des Américains, après quinze ans d’effacement
lemonde.description: Le conseiller spécial du président Donald Trump Massad Boulos cherche un accord entre les familles Haftar et Dbeibah, qui se partagent le pays.

lemonde.title: « Tous ces migrants illégaux qui arrivent sur nos côtes prennent les emplois des Britanniques » : dans la station balnéaire de Jaywick, le vote pour Nigel Farage est nourri par la peur de l’étranger
lemonde.description: Déstabilisé par la révélation d’un don non déclaré, le chef de Reform UK a provoqué une élection législative partielle en démissionnant et en cherchant à se faire réélire dans sa circonscription de Clacton-on-Sea. Travaillistes et conservateurs ont décidé de boycotter le scrutin, prévu jeudi 13 août.

lemonde.title: Aides sociales et avantages fiscaux des familles : un rapport propose 4,2 milliards d’euros d’économies sur ces dispositifs
lemonde.description: Dans un rapport commandé par le gouvernement et dévoilé fin juillet, l’inspection générale des finances et l’inspection générale des affaires sociales proposent d’améliorer la « cohérence » des politiques familiales.

lemonde.title: « Ils me glissent une écharpe de Miss autour de l’épaule et m’invitent à m’asseoir sur le trône » : le pot de départ royal de Muriel, employée d’un hypermarché
lemonde.description: « Bon vent ! » (9/18). Un tour en transpalette dans le Leclerc de Sarrebourg (Moselle), assise sur le fauteuil du Père Noël : dans la grande surface où elle a travaillé toute sa vie, Muriel Jamet, 63 ans, a eu droit à tous les honneurs.

lemonde.title: EN DIRECT, PSG-Aston Villa : Maghnes Akliouche titulaire pour sa première avec le club de la capitale
lemonde.description: Les Parisiens, vainqueurs de la Ligue des champions, lancent officiellement leur saison et leur quête de trophées mercredi à Salzbourg (Autriche), face aux Anglais, lauréats de la Ligue Europa.

lemonde.title: EN DIRECT, guerre en Ukraine : l’ONU a appelé la Russie à lever l’interdiction faite au seul parti antiguerre de participer aux élections législatives
lemonde.description: La Cour suprême russe a interdit, mardi, au parti Iabloko de participer aux élections. Son chef, Nikolaï Rybakov, avait annoncé qu’il ferait appel de la décision. La plupart des opposants au président Vladimir Poutine sont emprisonnés, en exil ou morts, et Iabloko est le seul parti libéral encore en activité en Russie.

lemonde.title: Cinquante ans après l’adoption de la loi fondatrice pour la protection de la nature, des avancées majeures aujourd’hui attaquées
lemonde.description: Les flamants roses, le castor et de nombreux rapaces ont bénéficié du texte promulgué en juillet 1976, qui a notamment instauré un régime de protection des espèces et reconnu la sensibilité animale. Les associations dénoncent la multiplication des accrocs.

lemonde.title: En Chine, un embryon congelé issu d’une relation extraconjugale défie la justice
lemonde.description: Le combat d’une épouse trompée, confrontée à l’obsession de son mari pour un nouvel héritier, révèle l’absence de statut juridique de l’embryon congelé.

lemonde.title: Jean-Michel Aulas a déposé un recours contre le retrait de sa délégation à la Métropole de Lyon
lemonde.description: A la mi-juin, la présidente de la Métropole de Lyon avait annoncé le retrait temporaire des délégations de M. Aulas et de deux autres élus après une plainte pour viol déposée par une militante d’une vingtaine d’années contre le directeur de communication du candidat.

lemonde.title: Pédopornographie : des milliers d’images et des dizaines de vidéos découvertes chez un assistant d’éducation à Vesoul
lemonde.description: L’homme a reconnu les téléchargements et la détention des divers objets et gadgets, tous à connotation sexuelle, en relation avec des mineurs. « Aucun signalement relatif à son comportement à l’égard d’élèves n’a été porté à la connaissance de l’établissement ou des services académiques dans le cadre de ses fonctions », a précisé le rectorat de Besançon.

lemonde.title: En Europe, les stocks de gaz pour l’hiver, au plus bas, ravivent les craintes sur les prix fin 2026 et début 2027
lemonde.description: Le taux de remplissage actuel des réserves européennes est inférieur à 60 %, contre près de 75 % ces deux dernières années, notamment en raison de prix estivaux élevés liés au blocage du détroit d’Ormuz.

lemonde.title: Iran : une trentaine de pays, dont la France, le Royaume-Uni et le Canada, condamnent les exécutions de manifestants

lemonde.title: « Mon stage chez les vieux », sur France.tv : trois lycéens en immersion dans le quotidien d’un Ehpad
lemonde.description: Delphine Corrard a suivi des jeunes entre 16 et 18 ans contraints de passer quatre semaines aux côtés de personnes âgées. L’expérience, à la fois surprenante, touchante et gaie, montre que parfois forcer le destin a du bon.

lemonde.title: Au Festival de Salzbourg, « Ariane à Naxos » explose en plein vol spatial
lemonde.description: Pour sa première participation à la manifestation d’art lyrique, le metteur en scène allemand d’origine turque Ersan Mondtag déçoit. Grevée par la direction routinière de Manfred Honeck, la partie musicale, malgré une distribution de qualité, ne parvient pas à s’imposer.

euronews.description: Renting an 80-square-metre home in Spain costs an average of 1,131 euros a month, but regional disparities are stark: from 600 euros in Jaen to 1,610 in San Sebastian.

euronews.description: "Maybe this is the time to realise WE ACTUALLY DON'T NEED AI," Brian May declared when posting a ridiculously poor version of what AI thinks one of Queen's albums looks like. He has urged UK Prime Minister Andy Burnham to block AI "before it's too late".

euronews.description: The world's two most watched oil forecasters published sharply conflicting views of 2026 on Wednesday, with the IEA deepening its call for the first annual demand decline since the pandemic while OPEC still sees consumption growing, as the closure of the Strait of Hormuz drags on.

euronews.title: Three Moroccan migrants arrested over alleged sexual assaults in Ceuta
euronews.description: Two men have been remanded in custody over alleged sexual assaults on minors, while a judge has ordered the deportation of a third.

Against the backdrop of the Infantino case, she identifies in an OpEd insights that can be applied to the corporate sector as a whole.

zeit.title: Russische Schattenflotte: »Haben Sie hier jemanden von Russland sprechen hören?«
zeit.description: In Hongkong steht ein chinesischer Kapitän vor Gericht, dessen Schiff Leitungen in der Ostsee zerstört haben soll. Manches erinnert an den Anschlag am Flughafen Leipzig.

Nachfolgerin von Steffen Bilger: Catarina dos Santos-Wintz soll neue Unions-Fraktionsmanagerin werden
zeit.description: Die Juristin Catarina dos Santos-Wintz soll die Fraktionsmanagerin der Unions im Bundestag werden. Sie würde damit dem neuen Verkehrsminister Steffen Bilger nachfolgen.

Landtagswahl: Grüne starten in Stäbelow in den heißen Wahlkampf
Bundestag: Dos Santos-Wintz soll neue Unions-Fraktionsmanagerin werden
Personalrochade: Dos Santos-Wintz übernimmt Schlüsselrolle in Unionsfraktion
Donald Trump: Organisationen verklagen Trump wegen Premiumzugangs zu Onlinedienst
zeit.description: Zwei Medienorganisationen reichen eine Klageschrift gegen US-Präsident Donald Trump ein. Der exklusive Zugang zu dessen Netzwerk sei »korrupt und verfassungswidrig«.

zeit.title: Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez: Sie macht mit ihrem Körper Politik
zeit.description: Die US-Politikerin Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez dokumentiert auf Social Media, dass sie ihre Eizellen einfrieren lässt. Und sofort gibt es große Aufregung. Das ist gut!

zeit.title: Ebola: WHO befürchtet in der DR Kongo schwersten Ebola-Ausbruch jemals
zeit.description: Die WHO sieht Anzeichen für ein nie dagewesenes Ausmaß der aktuellen Ebola-Epidemie in der DR Kongo. Die Organisation fordert eine bessere Gesundheitsversorgung vor Ort.

zeit.title: Orcas: Orca mit Schussverletzungen vor Gibraltar gesichtet
zeit.description: Vor Gibraltar haben Walschützer einen Schwertwal mit Schussverletzungen an der Rückenflosse beobachtet. Experten vermuten, dass mit Schrot auf den Orca gezielt wurde.

france24fr.title: Ebola en RDC : le cap des 2000 morts franchi
france24fr.description: En RDC, l’épidémie d’Ebola approche du bilan le plus meurtrier jamais enregistré dans le pays. Le virus a déjà fait 2 011 morts sur 4 381 cas confirmés, contre 2 300 décès lors de l’épidémie de 2018-2020. Les autorités congolaises estiment que le pic n’est pas encore atteint.

france24fr.title: LIBYE : Funérailles du chef des renseignements de Haftar tué dans un attentat
france24fr.description: 🇱🇾 En Libye, Fauzi al-Mansouri, chef des renseignements de l’Est a été tué lundi dans un attentat à la voiture piégée à Benghazi. Une attaque qui porte un coup au camp du maréchal Haftar, qui vise à étendre son contrôle sur la Libye.

france24fr.title: Éclipse solaire: quelles conséquences sur l'Environnement?
france24fr.description: L'éclipse solaire perturbe les activités de la faune, fait baisser la température et la force du vent. On passe en revue les effets de cette absence momentanée de lumière en plein jour sur l'Environnement.

france24fr.title: Éclipse : le gouvernement français avait-il distribué 35 millions de lunettes gratuites en 1999 ?
france24fr.description: Fustigeant la gestion gouvernementale de l'éclipse partielle de 2026, des personnalités politiques affirment que lors de l’éclipse solaire de 1999, le gouvernement français aurait distribué gratuitement 35 millions de paires de lunettes de protection. Si la mobilisation gouvernementale a été plus importante en 1999 qu'en 2026, plus de la moitié des lunettes avaient cependant été vendues par le secteur marchand.

france24fr.title: Rwanda : Nyakabingo, mine de tungstène stratégique pour la défense américaine.
france24fr.description: 🇷🇼 Au Rwanda, la mine de Nyakabingo est devenue en quelques mois l’un des principaux fournisseurs de tungstène des États-Unis. Ce métal stratégique, indispensable à l’industrie de défense, pourrait prendre une importance croissante alors que Washington prévoit de bannir les approvisionnements chinois destinés à ses usages militaires.

france24fr.title: Football : le PSG lance sa saison face à Aston Villa
france24fr.description: Le Paris Saint-Germain retrouve la compétition ce mercredi soir à Salzbourg, en Autriche, avec la Supercoupe d’Europe face à Aston Villa. Après une saison exceptionnelle et un deuxième sacre consécutif en Ligue des champions, les Parisiens ont l’occasion de poursuivre leur moisson de trophées face au vainqueur de la Ligue Europa. Récit de Julien Dubois.

france24fr.title: Fragilisé à la tête de la Fifa, Gianni Infantino "a de bonnes chances de passer l'été"
france24fr.description: Le président de la Fifa est dans l'œil du cyclone depuis l'annonce de son projet controversé d'ouvrir l'instance du football mondial à des investisseurs privés. Malgré un retrait rapide de ce projet, plusieurs confédérations, dont la puissante UEFA européenne, maintiennent Gianni Infantino sous pression. De quoi le pousser à la démission ? Rien n'est moins sûr d'ici la prochaine élection de la Fifa en mars prochain. Explications.

france24fr.title: Sécheresse en France : à Gérardmer, le lac bientôt pompé pour fournir l’eau potable
france24fr.description: À Gérardmer, dans les Vosges, le pompage de l’eau du lac débute ce mercredi 12 août pour alimenter le réseau d’eau potable. La baisse du niveau de la nappe phréatique ne permet plus de répondre suffisamment aux besoins des habitants et des communes voisines. Reportage France 2.

france24fr.title: En Cisjordanie, des colons israéliens assiègent des maisons palestiniennes
france24fr.description: Le siège d'habitations palestiniennes par des colons israéliens dans le nord de la Cisjordanie se poursuit mercredi, en dépit de l'intervention de l'armée israélienne. Celle-ci a dénoncé une "activité illégale" et "inacceptable".

france24fr.title: Omar Artan : privé du Mondial, il arbitre la Supercoupe d'Europe
france24fr.description: Privé de son rêve d'arbitrer au Mondial-2026 après avoir été refoulé des Etats-Unis en juin, le Somalien Omar Artan va diriger son premier match en Europe mercredi, invité par l'UEFA à arbitrer la finale de la Supercoupe d'Europe entre le Paris SG et Aston Villa.

france24fr.title: Addiction des mineurs : Meta face à la justice en Californie
france24fr.description: Meta comparaît devant un tribunal fédéral d’Oakland, en Californie. Quatre États américains accusent le groupe d’avoir conçu Instagram et Facebook pour rendre les mineurs dépendants, notamment grâce au défilement infini, aux notifications et aux mentions "J’aime". Décryptage de Mélina Huet.

france24fr.title: Séisme en Colombie : Pereira, une "ville zombie" en deuil national
france24fr.description: À Pereira, l’une des villes les plus durement touchées par le séisme de magnitude 7,4, les habitants tentent de retrouver leurs proches dans une ville privée d’électricité et lourdement dévastée. Correspondance de Maxime Pluvinet.

france24fr.title: Éclipse solaire : où et comment l’observer en France ?
france24fr.description: Horaire, ampleur et visibilité : tous les spectateurs ne verront pas l’éclipse de la même manière selon leur lieu d’observation. Tour d’horizon des conditions pour profiter au mieux du phénomène, sans oublier les indispensables lunettes de protection. Reportage France 2.

france24fr.title: Nigeria : le village d’Orimedu menacé par l’érosion côtière
france24fr.description: Orimedu est une communauté de pêcheurs située sur le littoral de l'État de Lagos, au Nigeria. Ce village fait face à une grave menace d'érosion côtière et de montée des eaux,  qui détruisent les habitations et mettent en péril les moyens de subsistance des habitants. Les communautés et les chercheurs tentent de trouver des solutions pour affronter le phénomène. Nicolas Chamontin.

france24fr.title: Des tonnes de méduses forcent EDF à arrêter trois réacteurs de la centrale nucléaire de Gravelines
france24fr.description: À Gravelines, dans le nord de la France, l’arrivée massive de méduses a contraint EDF à arrêter trois des six réacteurs de la centrale nucléaire. Plusieurs tonnes de méduses ont saturé les systèmes de filtration d’eau de mer qui alimentent la centrale. Un épisode qui intervient dans un été déjà marqué par les fortes chaleurs et les perturbations du parc nucléaire français.

france24fr.title: Au Nigéria, le village d'Orimedu menacé par l'érosion côtière
france24fr.description: À Orimedu, village de pêcheurs sur le littoral de l’État de Lagos, au Nigeria, l’érosion côtière et la montée des eaux gagnent du terrain. Des maisons sont endommagées et les activités de pêche menacées. Habitants et scientifiques expérimentent des réponses face à cette urgence.

france24fr.title: Rwanda : la mine de Nyakabingo, nouvel atout stratégique pour les États-Unis
france24fr.description: Au Rwanda, la mine de Nyakabingo est devenue en quelques mois l’un des principaux fournisseurs de tungstène des États-Unis, un métal stratégique indispensable à l’industrie de défense. Alors que Washington s’apprête à bannir tout approvisionnement chinois destiné à ses usages militaires, Kigali mise sur la mécanisation et la traçabilité pour s'imposer durablement sur ce marché. Un reportage d'Aurore Bayoud.

france24fr.title: Le Vietnam tente d'enrayer la chute de sa natalité
france24fr.description: Le Vietnam, pays de plus de 100 millions d’habitants, voit sa natalité chuter : autrefois terre de naissances et de familles nombreuses, il présente désormais un taux de fécondité tombé à 1,9 enfant par femme. Un chiffre qui inquiète le gouvernement, longtemps obsédé par le contrôle des naissances. En effet, pendant plus de 40 ans, la politique des deux enfants par famille était la norme au Vietnam. Mais cette interdiction a été levée en juin 2025.

spiegel.title: Eurovision Song Contest: Ausrichter kann Siegerländer als Gastgeber ausschließen
spiegel.description: Wer den Eurovision Song Contest gewinnt, darf im nächsten Jahr die große Party zu sich ins Land holen. Mit einer neuen Regelung hält der Ausrichter es sich ab sofort offen, bestimmte Länder als Gastgeber auszuschließen.

spiegel.title: Rechtsextremismus: Kinderzimmer-Nazis – immer jünger, immer radikaler - SPIEGEL TV
spiegel.description: Versuchter Mord, gefährliche Brandstiftung, Mitgliedschaft in einer terroristischen Vereinigung. Der jüngste Täter der rechtsextremen Gruppe »Letzte Verteidigungswelle« war zum Tatzeitpunkt 14 Jahre alt. Ihre Taten filmten sie selbst.

spiegel.title: Reform der Geheimdienste: Mehr Macht für BND und Verfassungsschutz, mehr Aufsicht
spiegel.description: Es ist richtig, dass die deutschen Geheimdienste mehr Befugnisse bekommen. Die Gefahr durch Russland ist real. Doch mehr Macht erfordert auch mehr Kontrolle.

spiegel.title: Matthias Lilienthal über das »Volksbad«: »Die Duschen sind aktuell nicht funktionsfähig«
spiegel.description: Gerade eröffnete die Berliner Volksbühne ein Schwimmbad, nun muss es schon wieder vorübergehend schließen. Intendant Matthias Lilienthal über die Gründe – und seine Idee, ins »Volksbad« stundenweise nur nichtweiße Menschen zu lassen.

spiegel.title: »The End of Oak Street«: Anne Hathaway und Ewan McGregor im Dino-Chaos
spiegel.description: In »The End of Oak Street« mit Anne Hathaway und Ewan McGregor wird eine Musterfamilie aus den Achtzigerjahren in die Ära der Dinosaurier versetzt. Gruselig? Ja, aber auch so albern, dass man sich gut unterhalten fühlen kann.

spiegel.title: WNBA: »MAGA-Barbie«, Trans-Hass und »White Privilege« – wie Sophie Cunningham den US-Basketball ins Chaos stürzt
spiegel.description: Die Debatten über die US-Liga WNBA drehen sich um alles außer Basketball: Ob trans Frauen gegen Frauen spielen dürfen oder ob weiße Spielerinnen bevorzugt werden. Das Gesicht der Absurdität ist Sophie Cunningham.

spiegel.title: Rekord: Dieser Wagen mit Wasserstoffantrieb fährt mehr als 650 km/h
spiegel.description: Im US-Bundesstaat Utah stellt der »JCB Hydromax« einen Geschwindigkeitsrekord für Autos mit Wasserstoff-Verbrennungsmotor auf. Am Steuer saß Andy Green, der 1997 als erster Mensch auf vier Rädern die Schallmauer durchbrach.

spiegel.title: Sonnenfinsternis heute im Livestream: Sehen Sie, wie es plötzlich dunkel wird
spiegel.description: Die Sonnenfinsternis naht – und Sie brauchen weder eine Spezialbrille noch ein Flugticket nach Mallorca, wo das Ereignis am besten zu sehen sein wird. Sie müssen nicht mal vom Sofa aufstehen: Hier ist der Livestream.

spiegel.title: Ehemaliger Premier Zhu Rongji ist tot: Chinas unbequemer Modernisierer
spiegel.description: Zhu Rongji reformierte Staatsbetriebe, als Premierminister führte er China in die Welthandelsorganisation – und sprach so offen, wie es unter Xi Jinping undenkbar wäre.

spiegel.title: Waldbrände in Deutschland und Europa: Wo es gerade brennt - Live-Grafiken
spiegel.description: Wie außergewöhnlich ist die aktuelle Waldbrandsaison, wo brennt es derzeit und wie viele Flächen sind den Flammen schon zum Opfer gefallen? Der fortwährend aktualisierte Überblick in Karten und Grafiken.

spiegel.title: Hessen: Spaziergänger findet qualmende Phosphorgranate am Rheinufer
spiegel.description: Plötzlich qualmte es am Rheinufer: Ein Mann hat im südhessischen Trebur ein Kampfmittel aus dem Zweiten Weltkrieg entdeckt. Solche Funde könnten laut Polizei angesichts der Niedrigpegel häufiger vorkommen.

spiegel.title: Reit-WM: Isabell Werth und das deutsche Team gewinnen Gold in der Dressur
spiegel.description: Die deutsche Dressur-Equipe um Isabell Werth hat bei den Reitsport-Weltmeisterschaften in Aachen zum 13. Mal den Titel gewonnen. Dabei hatte das Team vor Turnierbeginn auf zwei Stars verzichten müssen.

spiegel.title: News des Tages: Taifun in China, Erdbeben in Kolumbien und graue Autos in Deutschland
spiegel.description: In China räumen die Menschen die Schäden eines weiteren Taifuns auf, in Kolumbien suchen Rettungsteams nach Überlebenden des Erdbebens. Und in Deutschland fahren immer mehr graue Autos herum. Das ist die Lage am Mittwochabend.

spiegel.title: Los Angeles Lakers wechseln offenbar für 12 Milliarden Dollar den Besitzer
spiegel.description: Die Los Angeles Lakers sind eines der berühmtesten Sportteams der Welt. Nun wechselt die Basketballmannschaft erneut den Besitzer – und das wohl für einen Rekordpreis.

spiegel.title: Israel: Steffen Seibert kritisiert israelische Siedlungspolitik scharf
spiegel.description: Angesichts zunehmender Gewalt gegen Palästinenser fordert der frühere Botschafter Steffen Seibert eine Veränderung der deutschen Israelhaltung: Man müsse sich stärker gegen die Siedlungspolitik stellen.

spiegel.title: Wie Rechtsextreme mit der Parole »Volksverräter« Stimmung machen
spiegel.description: In der Geschichte wurden Verräter oft grausam ermordet. Nach der Nazizeit verschwand der Verratsbegriff in Deutschland weitgehend. Inzwischen ist er wieder da – als Schmähung gegen demokratische Politiker.

spiegel.title: Mark Zuckerberg: Schauspieler Jeremy Strong will Sympathien für Meta-Chef wecken
spiegel.description: Der »Succession«-Star ist für ambitionierte Rollenaneignungen bekannt. In der Fortsetzung von »The Social Network« verwandelt sich Jeremy Strong in den Meta-Chef – und will dessen Standpunkt vertreten.

spiegel.title: USA: Moderater Demokrat David Crowley gewinnt Vorwahl in Wisconsin
spiegel.description: Eigentlich hatte er sich bereits aus dem parteiinternen Wahlkampf in Wisconsin zurückgezogen. Nun hat David Crowley doch gewonnen, wohl wegen der zu linken Politik seiner Kontrahentin.

nzz.title: DIE NEUESTEN ENTWICKLUNGEN - Waffenruhe im Gazastreifen: Vermittlerstaaten verurteilen Israels jüngste Angriffe im Gazastreifen
nzz.description: Die Waffenruhe zwischen Israel und der Hamas ist brüchig. Bis zu einem nachhaltigen Frieden im Nahen Osten ist es ein weiter Weg. Die wichtigsten Fragen und Antworten.

nzz.title: BILDSTRECKE - Sonnenfinsternis über Europa: die spektakulärsten Bilder
nzz.description: An diesem Mittwochabend schiebt sich der Mond vor die Sonne. In Grönland, Island, Spanien und im Norden Portugals wird man eine totale Sonnenfinsternis beobachten können, in der Schweiz und in Deutschland eine partielle. So erleben die Menschen das Ereignis.

nzz.title: Keine Bodycams mehr für die Kantonspolizei: Das Bundesgericht tadelt das Berner Polizeigesetz zum zweiten Mal
nzz.description: Drei Bestimmungen mit neuen Überwachungsmitteln streicht das Gericht aus dem Berner Gesetz. Auf die umstrittenste Frage aber tritt es nicht ein. Damit bleibt bezüglich Reitschule alles beim Alten.

nzz.title: LIVE-TICKER - Hitze in Europa: Bis zu 36 Grad – Hitzewelle in der Schweiz hält bis Samstag an +++ Pegelstände des Rheins fallen weiter – Rekordtief in Köln
nzz.description: Wo ist es zurzeit besonders heiss? Und was sind die Auswirkungen auf die Menschen und die Umwelt? Die neuesten Meldungen über Hitzerekorde, Dürren und Brände in Europa.

nzz.title: ORF in der Krise: Sparzwang und Millionenklage des Ex-Chefs
nzz.description: Wegen geplanter Kürzungsmassnahmen erwägt Österreichs öffentlichrechtlicher Sender eine Verfassungsbeschwerde gegen die Regierung. Derweil klagt der nach Vorwürfen der sexuellen Belästigung entlassene ehemalige Generaldirektor Roland Weissmann gegen seine Kündigung.

nzz.title: Nur mit 6 Millionen Franken, aber mit der «Grande Dame der Teilchenphysik»: So will Rösti den Gipfel zur künstlichen Intelligenz in Genf zum Erfolg machen
nzz.description: Im Juni 2027 findet in Genf der grösste KI-Gipfel statt. Da der Bund sparen muss, dürften aber nur wenige Staatschefs anreisen.

nzz.title: DIE NEUESTEN ENTWICKLUNGEN - Migrationskrise in Europa: Marokko warnt vor erneutem Migrationssturm nach Ceuta
nzz.description: Über die griechischen Inseln, die Balkanroute oder den Ärmelkanal versuchen neben den Fluchtbewegungen aus der Ukraine noch immer täglich Migranten, unter Lebensgefahr nach Europa zu gelangen.

nzz.title: INTERAKTIV - So teuer ist Ihr Einkauf bei Aldi, Rewe und Co. geworden
nzz.description: Sie haben das Gefühl, alles wird teurer? Vergleichen Sie Ihren Kassenzettel von heute mit dem gleichen Einkauf von 2022 in deutschen Supermärkten – und erleben Sie Ihren persönlichen Preisschock.

nzz.title: INTERAKTIV - Gasspeicher liegen deutlich unter Normalniveau – die aktuellen Zahlen zur Energieversorgung in Deutschland
nzz.description: Wie wirken sich Energiewende und globale Krisen auf Strom- und Gaspreise aus? Hier gibt es jeden Tag die aktuellen Zahlen.

nzz.title: DATENANALYSE - Wie beliebt ist Donald Trump?
nzz.description: Täglich aktualisierte Umfragewerte zeigen, wie die Amerikaner derzeit zur Amtsführung ihres Präsidenten stehen. Eine Übersicht in Grafiken.

nzz.title: Die Inflation in Deutschland ist zurück – und könnte bald ordentlich zulegen
nzz.description: Im Juli haben vor allem die Preise für Energie deutlich angezogen. Neben dem Krieg im Nahen Osten bedroht die Trockenheit die Stabilität.

nzz.title: Valérie Dittli lässt ihre Partei zappeln
nzz.description: Die Waadtländer Regierungsrätin verzögert den Entscheid, ob sie 2027 erneut kandidieren will. Mit Dittli hätte die Mitte keinen Allianzpartner. Derweil will die Partei Strafanzeige wegen Urkundenfälschung erstatten.

nzz.title: Höhenangst ist weit verbreitet – wer sie bekämpfen will, muss sich ihr stellen
nzz.description: Simon Messner, Sohn der Bergsteigerlegende Reinhold und selbst ein passionierter Alpinist, leidet an Höhenangst – wie viele andere Menschen. Er hat gelernt, damit umzugehen. Und sagt, wie man das schafft.

nzz.title: Jihad und Hitler – In Italien wird ein junger Jihadist verhaftet, der mit dem Nationalsozialismus sympathisiert
nzz.description: Die Generation Z dominiert mittlerweile die jihadistische Szene in Italien. Ein aktueller Bericht aus Rom zeigt: Auch Rechtsextremisten werden jünger – und die Grenzen zwischen den Ideologien verschwimmen.

nzz.title: Mindestens 44 Tote bei Bootsunglück in Simbabwe
nzz.description: Eine überfüllte Fähre kentert auf dem Karibasee in Simbabwe. Mindestens 44 Menschen sterben. Die Suche nach Überlebenden läuft weiter.

nzz.title: KOMMENTAR - Obstruktion im Hinterzimmer – die Debatte über die EU-Verträge beginnt mit einem Fehlstart
nzz.description: Dass die bürgerlichen Wirtschaftspolitiker beim Lohnschutz nicht auf die Nötigungen der Gewerkschaften eingehen, ist verständlich. Dass sie hingegen vom verhandelten Abkommen abweichen wollen, ist Verhinderungspolitik.

observador.title: 19h. PM já falou com Marcelo Rebelo de Sousa após entrada...
observador.description: Ex-Presidente da República sentiu-se mal durante férias em Monte Gordo, no Algarve, tendo sido assistido no local pelo INEM. Ainda, demitiu-se o médico oncologista de Évora acusado de negligência.

observador.title: Açores: PS diz que Governo corta apoios a eventos turísticos
observador.description: Com o turismo nos Açores a cair há nove meses consecutivos, o PS denuncia que o Governo Regional continua a suspender financiamentos a eventos nas várias ilhas, violando decisão parlamentar.

observador.title: Cisjordânia. Famílias cercadas por colonos desde domingo
observador.description: As famílias denunciam que a água e a eletricidade foram cortadas e que os bens alimentares estão a terminar. As IDF anunciaram a retirada dos colonos, mas a operação resultou em confrontos.

observador.title: Veja aqui o eclipse em direto
observador.description: O eclipse pode ser visto na totalidade no norte de Portugal, em Bragança, e em várias regiões espanholas. Esta é uma transmissão em direto de Arija, na província espanhola de Burgos.

observador.title: Portugueses não têm direito de ser xenófobos, diz Carrascosa
observador.description: D. Andrés Carrascosa recorda histórias de comunidades portuguesas que deixaram o país e diz que acolhimento de estrangeiros é central na mensagem evangélica. Assume que crise em Ceuta é complexa.

observador.title: Pisioneiros ucranianos relatam violência sexual e tortura
observador.description: Testemunho foi dado numa reunião do Conselho de Segurança da ONU, onde a organização confirmou maus-tratos "generalizados e sistemáticos" a prisioneiros ucranianos.

observador.title: Angola quer empresários brasileiros mas recusa implorar
observador.description: Angola disponibilizou 800 mil hectares para o estabelecimento de empresas brasileiras. O ministro da Agricultura e Florestas angolano diz que Angola espera do Brasil "tudo e mais alguma coisa".

observador.title: Jato e balões da NASA vão estudar atmosfera durante eclipse
observador.description: "Cientistas podem estudar a coroa solar de uma maneira que não se pode fazer de qualquer outro lugar no sistema solar", relata gestora do programa de eclipses da NASA.

observador.title: 18h. PM garante total transparência na compra das fragatas
observador.description: Chega deixa dúvidas sobre o negócio e acusa o Governo de falta de transparência no investimento. Ainda, foram resgatados com vida dois dos quatro portugueses desparecidos no mar ao largo da Croácia.

observador.title: Ébola. Epidemia pode tornar-se a pior da história no Congo
observador.description: Já é a segunda pior de que há registo, com 4.400 casos e mais de 2.000 mortos. Tedros admite que o surto "está muito à frente" e avança mais depressa do que qualquer outro anterior.

observador.title: João Baião estreia "O amor é assim" em outubro em Sintra
observador.description: A peça terá seis sessões no Teatro Tivoli, em Lisboa, entre os dias 16 e 20 de março de 2027. A peça acompanha João Baião, homem que, em segredo, consegue conciliar duas vidas.

observador.title: Isasa vence sexta etapa, Guérin perde segundos na liderança
observador.description: O espanhol da Euskaltel-Euskadi bateu Rui Oliveira e Francisco Campos. Artem Nych, bicampeão da prova, está agora a 49 segundos do líder Guérin.

observador.title: Discord: 3 dias para suspender diretos no Brasil
observador.description: Jovem terá sido induzida à automutilação e ao suicídio em grupos no Discord. Multa pode chegar a 8,4 milhões de euros.

observador.title: "O Irão tem-se mostrado irredutível"
observador.description: Maria Isabel Tavares afirma que Irão usa controlo do Estreito de Ormuz como vantagem nas negociações. A docente considera que entrada de drones russos no espaço aéreo aliado é uma provocação.

observador.title: O verão diferente mas "sem drama" do turismo no Algarve
observador.description: Ainda que praias e restaurantes estejam cheios, os números da hotelaria do Algarve mostram um cenário com menos portugueses. Há 470 milhões de euros no Fundo de Compensação do Trabalho.

observador.title: Lucy Davis diagnosticada com cancro da mama "incurável"
observador.description: A atriz britânica de 53 anos, conhecida por The Office da BBC, revelou no Instagram o diagnóstico feito há um ano e meio. A doença espalhou-se para os ossos.

observador.title: PJ detém mulher suspeita de atear cinco fogos em Tarouca
observador.description: Os incêndios postos sobre vegetação seca atingiram e colocaram em perigo áreas de significativa densidade florestal. Colocaram ainda em perigo pessoas e património.

observador.title: Comissão Europeia envia equipa a Ceuta para avaliar situação
observador.description: O comissário europeu para as Migrações, Magnus Brunner, disse que a Comissão Europeia continua a "fornecer todo o apoio necessário" a Ceuta e está disponível para "aumentá-lo ainda mais".

elpais.description: Solo han de usarse gafas de protección homologadas. En el ‘minuto decisivo’, mientras hay totalidad, podemos retirarlas para disfrutar al natural del fenómeno

elpais.title: Los ‘haters’ del eclipse: “Prefiero ir al cine antes que verlo”
elpais.description: Mientras para muchos será una ocasión excepcional para observar el fenómeno astronómico “más espectacular”, para otros, el mejor plan será hacer cualquier otra cosa

elpais.description: El recién posesionado Abelardo de la Espriella no activa un llamado a otros países, a pesar de los múltiples ofrecimientos

elpais.title: Leo Messi se despide de su padre con una carta conmovedora: “No sé cómo seguir”
elpais.description: El futbolista pone en duda el futuro de su carrera y revela que intentó alargar la participación de Argentina hasta la final del Mundial para que su padre, que falleció el sábado, pudiera recuperarse y viajar a Estados Unidos

elpais.title: La erupción del Etna desata el caos en los aeropuertos de Sicilia en plena temporada alta
elpais.description: La ceniza obliga a cerrar repetidamente las terminales de Catania y alcanza también Comiso, mientras miles de turistas tratan de reorganizar sus viajes

elpais.title: La inesperada unión de los hijos de Cindy Crawford y Richard Gere revive una de las historias de amor más fascinantes de Hollywood
elpais.description: Kaia Gerber y Homer Gere coinciden por primera vez como protagonistas de ‘The Shards’, la nueva serie de Ryan Murphy, devolviendo a la actualidad el recuerdo de una pareja que simbolizó como pocas el ‘glamour’ (y también la controversia) de la meca del cine en los noventa

elpais.title: 16 pueblos españoles que piden manga larga cuando cae la tarde
elpais.description: Ante veranos cada vez más calurosos debido al cambio climático, proponemos varios enclaves para huir de los días infernales y de las noches tropicales (a partir de 20ºC). Las localidades elegidas no superarán (o no por mucho) los 30ºC en la próxima semana, según las previsiones de la Aemet y eltiempo.es, y además ofrecen interesantes encantos patrimoniales y naturales

elpais.title: Mojete manchego, otra receta tradicional para combatir el calor a base de tomate
elpais.description: Fresco o en conserva, da igual mientras vaya acompañado de huevo duro, cebolleta, aceitunas, un buen aceite de oliva y pan para mojar, como su nombre indica

elpais.title: Cristiano Ronaldo y Georgina se casan en una ceremonia íntima acompañados de sus cinco hijos
elpais.description: El futbolista y la ‘influencer’ han compartido una publicación conjunta en Instagram en la que muestran sus respectivas alianzas de recién casados. Según un comunicado emitido por la pareja, la ceremonia civil ha tenido lugar este 11 de agosto en Cascais (Portugal)

elpais.title: El verano del eclipse del toples en la piscina
elpais.description: La policía de la moral está triunfando en muchísimos sitios y amargando el baño a muchas mujeres

elpais.title: El rey del bulo se arrima al Rey
elpais.description: El agitador Javier Negre se hace una foto con Felipe VI y dispara la indignación de amigos y enemigos

nyt.title: A Space Expert Hoped to Use the Eclipse as Science Class. The D.J.s Had Other Plans.
nyt.description: Mar Carretero-Castrillo, an astrophysicist, returned to her remote village in Spain to be in the path of totality. Hundreds of  partygoers came too.

nyt.title: Why Were Polls So Wrong in the Wisconsin Governor’s Race?
nyt.description: Francesca Hong, the democratic socialist running in Wisconsin’s Democratic primary for governor, had a double-digit lead in polls as recently as last week. Then she lost. What happened?

nyt.title: Hong’s Defeat in Wisconsin Shows the Limits of the Progressive Movement
nyt.description: Francesca Hong’s defeat in the Democratic primary for governor defied expectations and may have shown the democratic socialist wave cannot reach beyond urban centers.

nyt.title: Takeaways From the Wisconsin, Minnesota and South Carolina Primaries
nyt.description: A moderate won the closely fought Democratic primary for governor in Wisconsin, the latest contest between the party’s progressive and moderate wings.

nyt.title: With Trump Secretly Evacuated, Imperiled Air Force One Became a Flying Decoy
nyt.description: In response to a threat against the jet last month, the president was clandestinely removed in a catering container. But the plane was sent into the skies anyway with government employees and reporters onboard.

nyt.title: See How Trump’s Secret Air Force One Swap Unfolded
nyt.description: The extraordinary subterfuge was aimed at protecting an American president who has been in Iran’s cross hairs for years.

nyt.title: Gulf Oil Giants Are Spending Billions to Build Ways Around Strait of Hormuz
nyt.description: Even if a cease-fire materializes, Gulf exporters recognize that relying strictly on the Strait of Hormuz is a risk they can no longer take.

nyt.title: Walking the King Charles III England Coast Path, Now Open to All
nyt.description: Paul Theroux traced the British coastline in 1982 for his book “The Kingdom by the Sea.” This year he walked parts of the new King Charles III England Coast Path, a continuous route along the country’s seashore.

nyt.title: Inflation Eased Slightly in July, but Prices Remain Elevated as War Drags On
nyt.description: Though energy prices fell last month after their spring surge, other factors pushed up costs as the Fed considers raising interest rates.

nyt.title: Benign Inflation Data Offers Reprieve to Fed as It Weighs Rate Increase
nyt.description: The latest Consumer Price Index report helped to reinforce the patient approach adopted by many officials at the Federal Reserve about raising rates, but it has not resolved the debate altogether.

nyt.title: ICE Agent Points Gun at Woman in Car in Virginia, Videos Show
nyt.description: The agent accused the woman of trying to run him over with her vehicle, a claim she denied. It was the latest tense encounter between a federal agent and a driver.

nyt.title: RFK Jr. Stirred Vaccine Fears in Pennsylvania Years Before Measles Outbreak
nyt.description: At a speech in Lancaster County, Robert F. Kennedy mocked the threat of measles. Now local officials are racing to contain one of the largest outbreaks in the country.

nyt.title: What to Know About the Vaccines Targeted by Trump’s Executive Order
nyt.description: The order, whose legal power is unclear, recommended narrowing the use of vaccinations against several diseases that can be life-threatening.

nyt.title: Even With Space Cops and Magic Rings, ‘Lanterns’ Keeps It Real
nyt.description: HBO’s next big bet in the DC Universe is more like a buddy-cop drama than the usual comic-book adaptation. Fans are in for a few surprises.

nyt.title: He Was Deported to Eswatini in Southern Africa. He May Never Go Free.
nyt.description: As the Trump administration sends a growing number of immigrants to countries they have no connection to, some find themselves imprisoned with no way out.

nyt.title: How a Reporter Interviewed Deportees Sent to a Prison in Africa by the Trump Administration
nyt.description: A Times reporter spoke with detainees in southern Africa using a cellphone one of them obtained after a hunger strike.

nyt.title: Effects of Record-Breaking El Niño Are Happening on 3 Continents
nyt.description: The recurring climate phenomenon is expected to peak later this year, but it is already causing dry spells and crop failures on three continents.

nyt.title: Europeans, Braced for 5th Heat Wave of 2026, Have Had Enough
nyt.description: With temperatures set to soar as high as 109 degrees Fahrenheit (43 Celsius) this week, Europeans and tourists say that summer in Europe has lost its appeal.

npr.title: Has the U.S. lost its dominance to China?
npr.description: Beijing may be benefiting from the war in Iran and Trump's tariffs and has an edge in the competition for tech supremacy. The New Yorker's Evan Osnos discusses his story "The Future, Made in China."

npr.title: Greetings from a surreal expanse of sand dunes dotted with freshwater lagoons in Brazil
npr.description: The pristine white sand dunes of the Lençóis Maranhenses National Park are bordered by thick jungle on one side and the Atlantic Ocean on the other. Thousands of lagoons fill up after the rainy season.

npr.title: Zhu Rongji, who drove China's 1990s economic reforms, has died at 97
npr.description: Zhu was renowned for reforms that sought to transition China from the post-Maoist years to a more global market-oriented financial system, without ceding party control over the economy.

npr.title: Takeaways from Tuesday primaries. And, Iran threat prompted Trump's secret plane swap
npr.description: Yesterday's primaries provided more insight into what voters in both parties want from their new leaders. And, Trump secretly switched planes in Turkey last month amid a foreign threat

npr.title: Andrew Tate's extradition fight tests his influence with Trump's America
npr.description: After President Trump took office, Andrew Tate proclaimed, "The Tates will be free." A year later, Tate is being held in federal prison after he was arrested following a U.K. extradition request.

npr.title: How a road could change West Africa's urban future
npr.description: A 600-mile journey along the shores of Nigeria, Togo, Ghana and Ivory Coast reveals one of the world's most consequential transformations.

npr.title: Former U.S. Marine held in Russia on disputed charges has been released
npr.description: Russia released an American military veteran, allowing his return to the U.S. after four years of what his family and U.S. officials allege was wrongful incarceration and abusive treatment.

npr.title: Earthquake response strains Colombia's new government and rescuers
npr.description: The earthquake killed at least 181 people and left 2,595 injured, according to Colombian authorities. At least 195 remained missing, but civilian-run databases put that number closer to 4,000.

npr.title: The death toll climbs from Monday's 7.4 magnitude earthquake in Colombia
npr.description: Hundreds of rescue workers have been deployed in hardest hit cities trying to free victims still trapped under the rubble. Hundreds of people are still missing.

npr.title: 1 year in, National Guard became a part of D.C. life. And, deadly quake hits Colombia
npr.description: Today marks one year since the National Guard was deployed to the nation's capital. Here's what has happened since. And, a 7.4 magnitude earthquake leaves more than 100 people dead in Colombia.

republika.description: Negli Stati Uniti prende forma un nuovo progetto. Obiettivo: contrastare il controllo massivo realizzato con l’IA. Un disegno stampato manderebbe in tilt le telecamere che cercano di individuare una persona o di leggere la targa di un’auto

phys-org.title: Ancient penguin fossils offer new window into Antarctica's changing climate
phys-org.description: A team of paleontologists from China University of Geosciences (Beijing) studying penguin fossils from Seymour Island off the Antarctic Peninsula have demonstrated how ancient bird bones can act as chemical archives of past climate change. The researchers used nondestructive X-ray mapping to examine the elemental composition of penguin remains spanning millions of years. phys-org.description: There is a question that often comes up at every public talk I do, and I have never had a good answer to it—well, not an entirely confident one. What's inside a black hole? The textbook reply is a singularity. Cross the event horizon, and everything falls inward to a point of infinite density where our equations return nonsense. It isn't so much an answer as an admission that we've run out of physics.

phys-org.title: Hybrid bioprinter creates capillary networks narrower than 10 micrometers
phys-org.description: More than 100,000 people are awaiting an organ transplant in the United States, with a new candidate added to the list every 10 minutes. Oxytocin is a hormone and neurotransmitter produced naturally in the body that influences social interactions, among other things.

phys-org.description: Whether it's neurons responding to electrical signals or plants stretching toward light, nature is filled with examples of biological materials that respond to their environment. Now, researchers want to develop new responsive materials for a wide range of applications, such as sensing or low-energy technologies. However, achieving a balance of useful properties at the molecular level is challenging.

phys-org.description: Modern biomedicine increasingly relies on enormous amounts of image data. Although computers can do part of the analysis work, biologists often still need to look through the images themselves. This takes time.

phys-org.title: Famous oddball quasar isn't X-ray weak after all, astronomers say
phys-org.description: For more than two decades, the quasar PHL 1811 has been considered the prototype of a rare class of "intrinsically X-ray weak" quasars, thought to produce unusually little X-ray radiation. But in 2024, the Einstein Probe spacecraft caught the object in a bright X-ray flare. In a new study, astronomers combined that observation with more than 20 years of archival data to revisit the mystery. The findings were published in The Astrophysical Journal on July 28.

phys-org.title: Human clinicians outperform AI stethoscope in diagnosing pet heart problems
phys-org.description: Fourth-year veterinary students matched—and experienced clinicians outperformed—an AI-enabled digital stethoscope in diagnosing heart murmurs and arrhythmias in cats and dogs, according to a new study from North Carolina State University. The study emphasizes the importance of human expertise when using AI-assisted technology, particularly with instruments designed for "universal" usage. The research is published in the Journal of the American Veterinary Medical Association.

This development, published today, Aug. 12, in The Journal of Immunology, offers a major step forward in sustainable farming and the global fight against antibiotic resistance.

phys-org.title: Online conflict may strengthen, not weaken, social movements, researchers find
phys-org.description: Online conflict tends to advance social movements rather than undermine them, according to new research from McGill's Desautels Faculty of Management.

phys-org.title: Spontaneous magnons synchronize with external signals at room temperature
phys-org.description: Signals ride on waves of one kind or another: light, sound, radio. But new carriers are needed to relay information in next-generation devices. Disturbances or waves in magnetic materials called magnons could be an efficient option—if scientists can tame them.

undark.description: In “The Beasts of the East,” journalist Andrew Moore charts the natural history of the East and the people who have dedicated their careers to restoring several long lost species to what remains of their original habitats.

undark.title: Book Review: The Case for the AI-Powered Global Brain
undark.description: In “The God Test,” Robert Wright considers a future in which human consciousness becomes infused with AI. “We have to think seriously about a future in which there is something that increasingly resembles a global brain, and its neurons increasingly consist not just of human brains but of AIs,” he writes.

undark.title: Interview: How Tragedy Changed the FDA

Sekeres, a scientist and former adviser, discusses the history and nuances of FDA oversight, including its process for screening advisory committee members for conflicts of interest.

undark.title: Will AI Fix Prior Authorization — or Make It Worse?
undark.description: The Trump administration is currently piloting a program in six states that expands Medicare prior authorizations using AI tools in an effort to reduce unnecessary medical spending. But it remains to be seen whether this new approach, which the administration has called “broken” in the private sector, will be effective without causing dangerous delays for Medicare recipients.

undark.title: Biologists Should Articulate Their Position on AI
undark.description: Last month, mathematics researchers released the Leiden Declaration, a treatise on how to handle the challenges that artificial intelligence poses to their field. C. Brandon Ogbunu argues that biologists should learn from the mathematics community and work on their own version.

undark.title: Review: What Animals Can Teach Humans About Caregiving
undark.description: From seahorses and birds to beetles and killer whales, journalist Elizabeth Preston finds a lot of common ground  between human and animal parenting in “The Creatures’ Guide to Caring,” a sweeping survey of the evolution of caregiving and the dizzying array of survival strategies in the animal kingdom.

undark.title: The MAHA Movement’s Worrisome Embrace of Ibogaine
undark.description: The MAHA movement has been promoting the plant-based substance ibogaine as a remedy for opioid addiction, despite the lack of clinical trials on its safety and efficacy. One physician who practices addiction medicine discusses the risks of ibogaine and argues for the need to support proven treatments.

undark.title: Advocacy Groups Express Mixed Views on Embryo Editing
undark.description: At least two new start-up companies, Preventive and Origin Genomics, say they are developing strategies that combine gene editing with in vitro fertilization to correct disease-causing mutations. Advocacy groups for people living with these genetic disorders have been quiet on the developments.

undark.title: Interview: California Lawmaker Calls for a Peptide Working Group
undark.description: Amid a national push to ease restrictions on certain peptides, California legislator Joe Patterson has introduced a state-level bill that would to establish a working group tasked with making recommendations to allow physicians and hospitals, among others, to prescribe and study promising peptides.

undark.title: Making Sense of Data From Wearable Health Trackers
undark.description: Wearable health devices such as smartwatches, glucose monitors, and sleep trackers are blurring the line between consumer wellness and clinical medicine. One physician argues that validation standards and privacy protections must be established to ensure the usefulness of the data these devices generate.

proj-syn.title: Europe Failed the Ceuta Test
proj-syn.description: The current migration crisis is eating away at the solidarity on which the European Union depends, fueling the rise of the far right and pushing leaders to adopt increasingly hardline policies. But the Ceuta debacle shows why such measures cannot address the deeper forces driving migration.

proj-syn.title: The Legacy of Zhu Rongji
proj-syn.description: Zhu Rongji’s personal history and political challenges made it highly unlikely that he would rise to the pinnacle of Chinese politics. Once there, he implemented many of the reforms that turned the country into an economic powerhouse.

proj-syn.title: The Twilight of the ICC
proj-syn.description: Born amid the euphoria of the West’s Cold War victory, the International Criminal Court embodied the aspiration that international law could transcend politics. But the ICC always represented victors’ justice, and it was never equipped to operate in a world shaped by Machtpolitik.

proj-syn.title: Will Latin America Embrace Guerrilla Geopolitics?
proj-syn.description: The resurgence of guerrilla warfare in Ukraine and Iran has underscored the potential benefits of asymmetric action in today’s increasingly multipolar world. Latin America, in particular, should consider how to leverage its many strengths to remedy its relatively weak position on the global stage.

proj-syn.title: China’s Biggest Weakness on AI
proj-syn.description: When a state can credibly promise that labor displacement will not mean destitution, workers and their representatives are more likely to accept technological change. But since China can promise no such thing, its lack of a robust welfare state has emerged as a fundamental weakness in the broader AI race.

proj-syn.title: The Monetary Roots of Political Extremism
proj-syn.description: While the global economy generates unprecedented wealth for plutocrats like Elon Musk, it is, by design, highly unequal, dangerously over-indebted, prone to recurring financial crises, and ecologically disastrous. In such a context, radical reforms will be needed, beginning with the rejection of money as a commodity.

proj-syn.title: The Return of the Power Trust
proj-syn.description: A century ago, the US power industry was dominated by sprawling, heavily indebted holding companies until their collapse forced the federal government to break them up. Now, the pattern is repeating, with mega-mergers and buyouts advancing a debt-heavy business model at the expense of households and communities.

proj-syn.title: Morocco’s Bet on Targeted AI
proj-syn.description: Rather than join the global race for computing power, Morocco has focused on building sovereignty over its data, talent, and uses of AI, because technological power will be measured by usefulness, not by domination. This strategy calls for the country to embrace innovation without ceding its identity to foreign models.

proj-syn.title: Dude, Where’s My Recession?
proj-syn.description: Despite a series of major negative shocks, some of them unprecedented, the US economy continues to grow in line with its estimated long-run potential. Yet given obvious and mounting risks, from debt-financed speculation to geopolitical tensions, the appearance of resilience should not be confused with the real thing.

proj-syn.title: The Rise of the Token Economy
proj-syn.description: Millions of people continuously generate the raw material on which AI is trained, yet almost none shares in the wealth it creates. This underscores the need for data cooperatives representing internet users, creators, and other rights holders to negotiate access to the content being fed to large language models.

proj-syn.title: Excess Savings Are Driving the New China Shock
proj-syn.description: The current China shock combines continued supply upgrading with an absorption problem: the decline in property and related investment has reduced domestic demand, but national saving remains very high. The result is a larger savings-investment surplus that spills into net exports.

proj-syn.title: The World Economy Is Swerving, and the Destination Is Unknown
proj-syn.description: The days of unfettered globalization, multilateral rule of law, commonly accepted limits on economic statecraft, and widely shared macroeconomic objectives are now long gone. A perpetual, directionless transition is our new reality, and corporate executives, investors, and policymakers must adapt accordingly.

proj-syn.title: Is China Really a Beggar-thy-Neighbor Power?
proj-syn.description: When major economies are running at near full capacity, it is not clear that trade deficits should be a cause for concern, since they represent a transfer of purchasing power from surplus countries. Under the current circumstances, then, China’s widely criticized surpluses might as well be called enrich-thy-neighbor.

proj-syn.title: No Escape from the Russian Terror Playbook
proj-syn.description: When Vladimir Putin revives Stalin-era repression tactics, he does not do so in service of some lofty ideology or grand project. Rather, he and his security apparatus are seeking to safeguard their own power indefinitely—and, as Russians well know, they will stop at nothing to succeed.

proj-syn.title: The Extractive Trap Has a Green Exit
proj-syn.description: For resource-rich developing countries, decades of resource extraction have produced income concentration, economic dependency, external vulnerabilities, and the weakening of other productive sectors. Achieving broad-based prosperity requires a new approach, one which leverages South-South cooperation to build green industries.

proj-syn.title: The Last Trump Election
proj-syn.description: No matter what US President Donald Trump says or does in response to the results of this November’s midterms, he will have faced his final popular vote. There will be further damage done to public confidence in American democratic institutions, but the institutions themselves will hold.

proj-syn.title: The Ceuta Crisis Is About More Than Migration
proj-syn.description: When tens of thousands of people recently entered the Spanish enclave of Ceuta from neighboring Morocco, European leaders lapsed into recriminations, reigniting the debate on migration. But the bigger challenge is to address a long-simmering territorial dispute between Spain and Morocco.

proj-syn.title: The Rising Price of a Cheap Renminbi
proj-syn.description: Renminbi appreciation would not, on its own, rebalance China’s economy and eliminate its massive surpluses. But by increasing households’ purchasing power over imports and compressing tradable-sector margins, it would raise the cost of avoiding reform.
